title: Viscardi-Reynaud packaging, metrology, conservation and shipment leads

source_context.guard: Email statements are retained as high-value research leads. They are not silently converted into archival facts where the underlying invoice, database field, object, packing material, dimension record or condition documentation has not yet been inspected.

source.title: Blaschka invertebrate models in Irish institutions
source.journal: Journal of the History of Collections

verified_relevance: The study converted archival order documents into Word and Excel for analysis.
The located 1882 NMI and 1885 UCD invoices list scientific names, Ward catalogue numbers and individual model prices.
The invoices also break down the overall order cost, including packaging, transport and boxes.
The published research therefore already contains a structured invoice/packing-cost layer, although it does not reconstruct transport as a full handoff history.

new_leads_from_reynaud_email.claim: The database contains a long list of associated packaging elements that were notified to customers as additional shipment costs.
questions: Are packaging fields attached to individual models, inner boxes, outer cases, orders or shipments?
Which archival document genres generated these fields?
Are original wording and charges retained alongside normalized terms?

new_leads_from_reynaud_email.claim: The Blaschkas used local measures and a Dresden foot was not equivalent to a British or Frankfurt foot.
new_leads_from_reynaud_email.research_value: Potentially converts crate dimensions from apparently comparable numbers into a metrological-translation problem across workshop, commercial and receiving records.
new_leads_from_reynaud_email.proposed_transformation: local workshop measure -> transport/commercial measure -> receiver interpretation
questions: What exact source establishes the unit system?
Are dimensions stored in original units before conversion?
Does the database preserve the conversion rule and uncertainty?

new_leads_from_reynaud_email.claim: An elaborate support system used cardboard bases and wires, with cork elements; some models had flatter sides and boxes varied in size.

current_backend_comparison.cardboard_support: strongly documented in later Harvard transport procedure
current_backend_comparison.wire: common in model construction/support records but transport-specific use must be demonstrated separately
current_backend_comparison.cork: new lead; no equivalent high-confidence packing evidence yet isolated in current backend
current_backend_comparison.variable_box_size: plausible and consistent with shipment architecture but requires source-level matching

new_leads_from_reynaud_email.guard: Do not infer that all wire mentioned in object construction records functioned as packing wire.

new_leads_from_reynaud_email.claim: Wood-shaving fill could be coarse or fine depending on the model.
new_leads_from_reynaud_email.research_value: Suggests filler was a calibrated mechanical variable tied to object form rather than generic waste packing.
questions: What source distinguishes coarse from fine shavings?
Is the distinction linked to catalogue number, geometry, fragility, price or case type?
Can one shipment be reconstructed model-by-model against filler type?

new_leads_from_viscardi_email.institution: World Museum Liverpool / historical Liverpool Museum
new_leads_from_viscardi_email.claim: The Liverpool Blaschka collection suffered after arrival; bombing destroyed some models and later storage conditions also caused problems.
new_leads_from_viscardi_email.existing_backend_guard: The current Liverpool module records severe May 1941 institutional wartime risk but intentionally leaves Blaschka-specific loss count unresolved.

new_leads_from_viscardi_email.claim: The collection was recently moved in its entirety across Dublin into bespoke storage; conservation for eventual redisplay is ongoing and Viscardi is writing a paper on the move.
new_leads_from_viscardi_email.research_value: Provides a contemporary comparator for repeated mobility of the same class of fragile objects: condition assessment, packing, transport, storage, conservation and redisplay.
new_leads_from_viscardi_email.guard: Use as a comparative mobility/conservation regime, not as direct evidence for nineteenth-century practice.

crosscheck_cases.problem: The relationship between 247 Marks, the approximately 50-Mark packing estimate and the later 268-Mark whole amount remains unresolved.
crosscheck_cases.guard: Do not calculate 21 Marks as the final packing charge solely from 268 minus 247.
crosscheck_cases.database_question: Does Reynaud's database contain this shipment/order or a related Damon entry with packaging fields capable of resolving the account layers?

crosscheck_cases.institution: Royal College of Science Dublin / Trinity College Dublin

primary_workshop_sequence.sollas_misrouting: shipment landed at Bristol because of mistake in shipper's note
primary_workshop_sequence.recovery: fresh examples included in Haddon's later consignment

crosscheck_cases.operational_chain: shipper's note error -> wrong port -> delay -> breakage -> replacement -> consolidation into another customer's shipment
crosscheck_cases.database_question: Can the Irish database recover the order contents, packing charges, replacement entries or object numbers around this failure chain?

known_sequence: four outer cases and twenty-seven framed boxes in 1929
packing materials, packing wages, railway transport and consular paperwork separated in the account
straw/hay becomes a U.S. plant-quarantine problem
1930 method uses cardboard supports, cardboard boxes, tissue immobilisation, pinewood outer boxes, straw and burlap
museum customs opening is followed by removal from temporary supports and plaster remounting
Ames feeds vibration and packing-material regulation knowledge back to Rudolf
1932 near-perfect arrival is explicitly linked by Rudolf to Louis Bierweiler's careful unpacking
crosscheck_cases.research_function: longitudinal control for testing whether the Irish packaging-element typology corresponds to actual transport, border and receiving outcomes

current_project_strengths: multiplex movement of people, models, specimens, drawings, seeds, money and documents
project_boundary.working_synthesis: Their material can supply a packaging vocabulary and database-level component structure; the current project can show how those components behaved once shipments entered transport, customs, receiving, storage, damage and repair regimes.

preferred_initial_data_request: one Irish invoice with full packaging/transport breakdown
one record demonstrating historical foot-unit conversion
one record showing cork and coarse/fine shavings at source level
research_observation: The strongest junction is between packing as a database of materials, dimensions and charges and transport as a sequence of transformations and handoffs. Liverpool supplies an accounting/survival cross-check, Dublin a misrouting/breakage/replacement chain, Harvard a longitudinal packing-customs-unpacking feedback control, while the new email leads add metrology, cork, shaving specification and post-arrival conservation/mobility questions that are currently underrepresented in the backend.
